title_en: Wang Guolin, Xiao Zhongcheng — case of sabotaging communication equipment
keywords_en: Criminal; Destruction of Communication Equipment; First Instance; Basic People's Court; Hubei Province; Natural Person; Criminal Law; Whether theft of military communication wires constitutes the crime of destruction of communication equipment; Support Plaintiff; Theft of military communication wires; During flood control and disaster relief; Communication interruption; Theft
full_text_en:
Wang Guolin, Xiao Zhongcheng — case of sabotaging communication equipment

Defendant Wang Guolin, male, 19 years old, former worker of the Wulidun Alloy Factory in Ezhou City, Hubei Province, arrested on July 14, 1991.

Defendant Xiao Zhongcheng, male, 19 years old, former worker of the Wulidun Alloy Factory in Ezhou City, Hubei Province, arrested on July 15, 1991.

The case of defendants Wang Guolin and Xiao Zhongcheng for sabotaging communication equipment was initiated by the Echeng District People's Procuratorate of Ezhou City, Hubei Province, which filed a public prosecution with the Echeng District People's Court. After conducting a public trial, the Echeng District People's Court found the following:

At a time when the general public of Hubei Province and the People's Liberation Army were engaged in flood control and disaster relief, defendant Wang Guolin, in the early morning of July 8, 1991, carrying tools such as pliers, went to the Xiaowanghe section of the Wuhan-to-Huangshi military communication line in Shishan Township and cut four spans (two phases) of 3.0-type copper military communication wires in use, totaling 400 meters. While Wang Guolin was coiling the wires, he was caught by a communications soldier of a certain PLA unit who was patrolling the line. Because the military communication line was cut by Wang Guolin, communications were interrupted for 190 minutes, causing significant losses.

One night in October 1990, defendant Wang Guolin, together with defendant Xiao Zhongcheng, carrying tools such as pliers, went to the Xiaowanghe section of the Wuhan-to-Huangshi military communication line. Wang Guolin cut the wires, and Xiao Zhongcheng coiled them, cutting one span (100 meters) of 2.5-type copper military communication wires in use.

The above facts are confirmed by documentary evidence, physical evidence, and witness testimony, and both defendants confessed to the crimes.

The Echeng District People's Court held that the defendants Wang Guolin and Xiao Zhongcheng stole military communication wires in use, endangering public safety, and their acts constituted the crime of sabotaging communication equipment as provided in Article 111, paragraph 1, of the Criminal Law of the PRC. In particular, at a time when heavy rainstorms had caused flooding in eastern Hubei in early July and the military and civilians were intensively engaged in flood control and disaster relief, defendant Wang Guolin stole military communication wires, causing a 190-minute communication interruption. The circumstances were odious and the consequences serious, warranting severe punishment. Wang Guolin's conduct seriously disrupted social order, and pursuant to Article 52 of the Criminal Law, deprivation of political rights may be imposed as a supplementary punishment. Accordingly, on July 24, 1991, the Echeng District People's Court rendered the following judgment:

Defendant Wang Guolin is convicted of the crime of sabotaging communication equipment and sentenced to thirteen years' imprisonment, with deprivation of political rights for three years;

Defendant Xiao Zhongcheng is convicted of the crime of sabotaging communication equipment and sentenced to five years' imprisonment.

After the first-instance judgment was announced, defendants Wang Guolin and Xiao Zhongcheng did not appeal.
